newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Red Cross agrees to food talks with North.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Red Cross agrees to food talks with North.

text.p: The South Korean Red Cross said it would hold talks with its North Korean counterpart for more food aid despite shooting across the border earlier this week.
The South Korean organisation sent a message to the North, saying it had accepted a Northern demand that the talks be held in Beijing next Wednesday, a Seoul Red Cross spokesman said on Friday.
"Food aid will continue," the spokesman told Reuters in response to a question whether Wednesday's border clash would have any impact on shipments of aid to the hunger-stricken North.

South Korea and the U.S.-led United Nations Command have protested to the North over the fierce exchange of fire at the Demilitarised Zone, that followed North Korean soldiers' intrusion into the South. The DMZ bisects the Korean peninsula.

The South Korean Red Cross, which is due to complete shipments of 50,000 tonnes of food aid to North Korea this month, plans to offer addition relief supplies in the proposed Beijing talks, the spokesman said.
The southern Red Cross society proposed last week to hold talks in the Korean peninsula on July 22 but the North counterproposed on Tuesday that the meeting be held in Beijing on July 23.
